tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local concurrency replay extending the prior claim/idempotency frontier. Claimant A owns logical operation O5 under claim record C4 with fence F4 and lease L4, then is delayed beyond lease expiry. Claimant B atomically takes over the same logical operation at strictly newer fence F5. The replay compares no-fencing, lease-only, and monotonic-fencing repository acceptance rules when stale A resumes. It tests repository-visible claim/publication safety and the limits of repository fencing for an external side effect; it does not verify any concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf.

common_state.failure_boundary: A is delayed past L4; B takes over and becomes authoritative; stale A later resumes while B may already be preparing, issuing, or finalizing the same logical operation

steps: A acquires C4 and begins work
A is delayed past lease expiry
B observes expiry and takes over
A resumes using only cached ownership and writes or issues the logical effect
B independently writes or issues the same logical effect
trace_no_fencing.observation: Nothing in the acceptance path distinguishes stale A from current B. Both can produce conflicting repository publications and, if an external effect exists, both can issue it.

steps: Ownership is represented by claimant identity plus an expiry timestamp but no monotonic generation/fence
B takes over after L4 expires
A resumes and performs a fresh timestamp/owner check before acting
A and B race between that check and the later publication or external effect
trace_lease_only.observation: A lease recheck narrows the race but does not itself bind a later effect or commit to the ownership version observed by the check. Repository publication can be made safer only if the final write CASes against an exact current claim version; an unfenced external effect can still be issued by stale A after authority moved to B.

steps: A acquires F4 and all prepared state records bind O5,D5,F4
B takeover atomically advances the claim to F5 and records B as current claimant
every repository publish/finalize transition requires CAS against exact predecessor identity plus current claim fence F5
stale A resumes with F4 and attempts a repository transition
the CAS/fence predicate rejects A because F4 is not current
B alone can publish/finalize repository state under F5
trace_monotonic_fencing.observation: For repository mutations in this exact replay, a strictly monotonic fence coupled to the final acceptance CAS prevents stale A from publishing after B becomes authoritative. Safety does not depend on A voluntarily noticing staleness.
trace_monotonic_fencing.external_effect_limit: Repository fencing alone cannot prevent stale A from sending a non-fenced external side effect after F5 exists. External duplicate safety additionally requires either provider-side rejection of lower fences or a stable logical-operation idempotency identity bound to O5 and D5 that remains valid across claimant handoff for the required recovery horizon.

minimum_repository_visible_contract: Stable logical operation identity O5 and exact payload digest D5 shared across retries and claimant handoff.
Claim record containing current claimant, monotonically increasing fence/generation, lease expiry metadata, and an exact CAS/version identity.
Takeover rule that atomically advances the fence; a fence value is never reused after authority moves forward.
Prepared/effect-committed/finalized stage bound to predecessor/successor generation identities, logical operation, payload digest, and the fence that authorized that transition.

Every repository publication/finalization must CAS both the exact predecessor/stage identity and the currently authoritative fence, so a stale claimant cannot commit merely because it still holds an old lease token.

If the logical operation has an external effect, duplicate safety requires provider-visible fencing or an idempotency identity stable across claimant transfer plus durable result/effect evidence; repository fencing by itself is not enough.

weak_lease_only_rule.rule: After a delayed claimant resumes, it may continue if a fresh lease/owner check appears valid; later effect issuance and publication need not carry the exact ownership generation observed by that check.
weak_lease_only_rule.falsification: A can pass the check immediately before B's takeover, then pause; B advances authority and acts; stale A resumes and its later unfenced action is still accepted or externally issued. The check and the effect are separated by a TOCTOU window, so the rule does not guarantee single-winner behavior.

observations: Lease expiry answers when takeover may begin; it does not by itself establish which claimant a later effect or commit belongs to.
The safety-critical fence check must occur at the irreversible acceptance boundary, not only at claim acquisition or a preflight reread.
Monotonic fencing makes stale repository publication rejectable even if the stale claimant behaves incorrectly, because acceptance is bound to the current generation.

For external side effects, a repository fence is only local evidence. Without provider-side fence enforcement or cross-claimant idempotency, a stale claimant may still cause an irreversible duplicate before the repository rejects its later commit.
inference: For the exact concurrent-expiry replay tested, the minimum repository claim protocol needs both a lease and a monotonic authority generation: the lease permits takeover, while the fence plus final CAS makes stale publication impossible after takeover. This closes the repository-local stale-writer race but not a non-fenced external-effect race. End-to-end duplicate safety therefore requires the irreversible external acceptance point to share the same authority generation or a stable idempotency identity/result contract that survives claimant transfer. This fixture does not prove that any concrete Chat-exposed zero-cost primitive supplies those semantics or that the Phase-1 root is satisfied.
unresolved_children: Verify a concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed repository/API primitive against the full claim/idempotency contract, including stable logical identity, payload binding, monotonic fencing or equivalent single-winner acceptance, result reconstruction, retention horizon, CAS/readback and absence of external arbitration or finite quota.

Test the hardest handoff window where stale A's external effect is accepted before A learns it lost F4, then B becomes authoritative at F5 before A can durably write the post-effect receipt; compare provider-fence enforcement versus a stable cross-claimant idempotency/result token and derive which receipt under which fence may be accepted.
